title_en: Regulations on the Protection of Varieties of Traditional Chinese Medicine

articles.content_en: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated to improve the quality of Chinese medicine varieties, protect the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese medicine production enterprises, and promote the development of the Chinese medicine industry.

Article 2 These Regulations shall apply to Chinese medicine varieties produced and manufactured within the territory of China, including Chinese patent medicines, extracts of natural medicines and their preparations, and artificial products of Chinese medicine.
Chinese medicine varieties for which a patent is applied shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of the Patent Law, and these Regulations shall not apply.

Article 3 The State shall encourage the research and development of clinically effective Chinese medicine varieties, and shall implement a graded protection system for Chinese medicine varieties with stable quality and definite therapeutic effects.
Article 4 The drug regulatory department of the State Council shall be responsible for the supervision and administration of the protection of Chinese medicine varieties nationwide.

Article 5 Chinese medicine varieties protected in accordance with these Regulations shall be those listed in the national drug standards. Varieties listed in the drug standards of provinces, autonomous regions, or municipalities directly under the Central Government, as determined by the drug regulatory department of the State Council, may also apply for protection.
Protected Chinese medicine varieties shall be classified into Grade I and Grade II.

Article 8 New drugs approved by the drug regulatory department of the State Council shall be granted protection in accordance with the protection period prescribed by the drug regulatory department of the State Council; where such drugs meet the provisions of Articles 6 and 7 of these Regulations, they may re-apply for protection in accordance with the provisions of these Regulations six months prior to the expiration of the protection period approved by the drug regulatory department of the State Council.

Article 9 The procedures for applying for protection of Chinese medicine varieties:
(1) A Chinese medicine production enterprise may file an application with the drug regulatory department of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government where it is located for a Chinese medicine variety produced by it that meets the provisions of Articles 5, 6, 7, and 8 of these Regulations; the drug regulatory department of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government shall conduct a preliminary examination and sign its comments, and then submit the application to the drug regulatory department of the State Council. Under special circumstances, the Chinese medicine production enterprise may also file an application directly with the drug regulatory department of the State Council.
(2) The drug regulatory department of the State Council shall entrust the National Chinese Medicine Variety Protection Review Committee with the responsibility of reviewing the Chinese medicine varieties applying for protection. The National Chinese Medicine Variety Protection Review Committee shall make a review conclusion within six months from the date of receiving the application report.
(3) Based on the review conclusion of the National Chinese Medicine Variety Protection Review Committee, the drug regulatory department of the State Council shall decide whether to grant protection. Chinese medicine varieties for which protection is approved shall be issued a "Certificate of Protected Chinese Medicine Variety" by the drug regulatory department of the State Council.
The drug regulatory department of the State Council shall be responsible for organizing the National Chinese Medicine Variety Protection Review Committee, whose members shall be appointed by the drug regulatory department of the State Council from experts in Chinese medicine in the fields of medical treatment, scientific research, inspection, and operation and management.

Article 10 An enterprise applying for protection of a Chinese medicine variety shall, in accordance with the provisions of the drug regulatory department of the State Council, submit complete materials to the National Chinese Medicine Variety Protection Review Committee.

Article 11 For Chinese medicine varieties for which protection is approved and those whose protection period expires, the drug regulatory department of the State Council shall make a public announcement in designated professional newspapers and periodicals.

Article 12 The protection period for protected Chinese medicine varieties:
Grade I protected Chinese medicine varieties shall be thirty years, twenty years, or ten years respectively.
Grade II protected Chinese medicine varieties shall be seven years.

Article 13 The prescription composition and technological process of Grade I protected Chinese medicine varieties shall be kept confidential by the production enterprise that has obtained the "Certificate of Protected Chinese Medicine Variety" and the relevant drug regulatory departments, relevant entities, and individuals within the protection period, and shall not be disclosed.
The relevant departments, enterprises, and entities responsible for confidentiality shall, in accordance with the relevant state provisions, establish necessary confidentiality systems.

Article 14 Where the prescription composition and technological process of a Grade I protected Chinese medicine variety are transferred abroad, the transfer shall be handled in accordance with the state provisions on confidentiality.

Article 15 Where a Grade I protected Chinese medicine variety needs to extend its protection period due to special circumstances, the production enterprise shall submit an application six months prior to the expiration of the protection period for such variety in accordance with the procedures prescribed in Article 9 of these Regulations. The extended protection period shall be determined by the drug regulatory department of the State Council based on the review results of the National Chinese Medicine Variety Protection Review Committee; however, each extension shall not exceed the initially approved protection period.

Article 16 A Grade II protected Chinese medicine variety may be extended for seven years after the expiration of its protection period.
A Grade II protected Chinese medicine variety applying for extension of protection shall be applied for by the production enterprise six months prior to the expiration of the protection period in accordance with the procedures prescribed in Article 9 of these Regulations.

Article 17 Protected Chinese medicine varieties that have been approved shall, within the protection period, be limited to production by the enterprise that has obtained the "Certificate of Protected Chinese Medicine Variety"; except as otherwise provided in Article 19 of these Regulations.

Article 19 The imitation of protected Chinese medicine varieties that are in short supply for clinical use shall be subject to approval by the drug regulatory department of the State Council, which shall also issue an approval number. The imitating enterprise shall pay a reasonable usage fee to the enterprise that holds the "Certificate of Protected Chinese Medicine Variety" and transfers the prescription composition and technological process of such Chinese medicine variety; the amount shall be negotiated by both parties. Where the parties fail to reach an agreement, the drug regulatory department of the State Council shall make a ruling.

Article 20 Enterprises producing protected Chinese medicine varieties shall, based on the requirements raised by the drug regulatory department of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government, improve production conditions and enhance the quality of varieties.

Article 21 Where application for overseas registration of a Chinese medicine protected variety is made during its protection term, approval from the drug regulatory department of the State Council shall be obtained.

Article 22 Where a person responsible for divulging secrets in violation of Article 13 of these Regulations, he shall be given an administrative sanction by his unit or the competent authority at a higher level; if his act constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 23 Where anyone, in violation of Article 17 of these Regulations, manufactures a counterfeit Chinese medicine protected variety without authorization, the drug regulatory department under the people's government at or above the county level shall punish it as manufacturing counterfeit drugs according to law.
Where anyone forges the Protection Certificate for Chinese Medicine Variety or relevant supporting documents for production or sale, the drug regulatory department under the people's government at or above the county level shall confiscate all relevant drugs and illegal gains, and may impose a fine of not more than three times the authentic price of the drugs concerned.
If any of the above acts constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated by the judicial organ according to law.

Article 24 Where a party is dissatisfied with the penalty decision made by the drug regulatory department, he may apply for administrative reconsideration or institute administrative action in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws and administrative regulations.
Article 25 The submission requirements and forms for application for Chinese medicine protected varieties shall be formulated by the drug regulatory department of the State Council.
Article 26 These Regulations shall come into force as of January 1, 1993.
